title: Interest & Compound Interest Methodology
overview: Understanding the difference between simple and compound interest is fundamental to financial planning. Compound interest is the 'eighth wonder of the world' - it can work for you (savings) or against you (debt).

methods.name: Compound Interest Formula
methods.description: Interest calculated on both the initial principal and accumulated interest from previous periods. The standard for most savings and investment accounts.

methods.name: Simple Interest Formula
methods.description: Interest calculated only on the original principal. Less common but used in some bonds and short-term loans.

methods.name: Continuous Compounding
methods.description: The mathematical limit of compounding as frequency approaches infinity. Used in financial modeling and some sophisticated products.
limitations: Difference from daily compounding is minimal

methods.name: Rule of 72 (Quick Estimation)
methods.description: A mental math shortcut to estimate how long it takes to double your money at a given interest rate.

formula.name: Rule of 72
formula.description: Example: At 8% interest, money doubles in ~9 years (72/8=9)

footnotes: Compounding frequency: Daily > Monthly > Quarterly > Annually
APY (Annual Percentage Yield) accounts for compounding; APR does not
The difference between daily and continuous compounding is negligible
Real return = Nominal return - Inflation rate
disclaimer: Interest calculations assume constant rates and don't account for taxes or fees. Actual investment returns vary and past performance doesn't guarantee future results.
